settings.body:
The Soccer package category helps myDreamshoots customers choose a clear package direction before they spend credits.

When Soccer is the right fit

Use Soccer when Soccer and Sports are the nearest match for the next photo set. If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest soccer requests keep the brief and the result aligned. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare clear approved source portraits, then add one cue that belongs to Soccer: light, scene texture, outfit tone, occasion, group size, or card-ready crop. Start with sharp source photos and one style cue that matters most to the package. Treat the source photos as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, fan details, holiday cues, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. myDreamshoots can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

How to compare Soccer with nearby choices

Compare soccer against neighboring packages by the job it solves, not by which cover image looks strongest. The table below turns the category into a practical choice before credit cost is confirmed.

Decision pointUse Soccer whenReview after generation
Final useUse Soccer when Sports is the right broad direction and the private album needs the specific look, scene, or keepsake format described by Soccer.Review whether the finished images look like Soccer instead of drifting into a generic Sports album.
source photosPrepare clear approved source portraits, then add one cue that belongs to Soccer: light, scene texture, outfit tone, occasion, group size, or card-ready crop.Check whether the clearest input details carried through the best images.
Category examplesSoccer and SportsKeep the outputs that match the chosen example instead of mixing several directions.
Credit planUse a focused first pass when the style is new.Decide whether the next request should repeat, expand, or change direction.

Credit and private gallery planning

Before the job starts, review the visible credit cost and ask whether the category is carrying the right amount of work. If you only need to test soccer, a smaller request can teach you what works. If the final use is already clear, a broader gallery may be easier to judge because it gives more crops and expressions to compare.

Finished outputs belong in the signed-in private gallery first. Use that space to compare identity, crop, expression, background detail, and whether the package category actually delivered the mood you selected. Download favorites only after separating public-use images from experiments.

Details to review before download

Review whether the finished images look like Soccer instead of drifting into a generic Sports album. Also check small visual details that often decide whether a result is ready for a profile, card, post, or archive: face consistency, hand and hair edges, clothing lines, background distractions, and whether the image still reads well at the crop size where you will use it.

Soccer should be recognizable through visible details such as color, posture, card framing, scene texture, seasonal cues, supporter energy, or private keepsake mood. This is where Soccer becomes more than a menu label. The visible mood should explain why the category was chosen, while the private gallery keeps the customer in control of what stays personal and what becomes a downloaded favorite.

Mistakes to avoid

Avoid asking Soccer to cover several unrelated fan, game-day, premiere, or holiday scenes at once; the narrower theme should make review easier. The fastest way to weaken soccer results is to overload the request with unrelated goals. Do not ask one job to be a professional portrait, a themed album, a restoration pass, and a motion concept at the same time. Keep the category honest, then run a second request when the next direction is different enough to need its own review.

A planning pass before you spend credits

  • Name the exact use for the finished images.
  • Choose the clearest source photos before adding style references.
  • Match the request to Soccer and Sports, not every nearby category.
  • Review credit cost before generation starts.
  • Use the private gallery to compare results before downloading favorites.

Start with Headshot Photo Package, then compare Soccer with nearby categories before generating. The best choice is the one that makes the review criteria obvious before the first image is generated.

Soccer FAQ

Soccer questions usually come down to source quality, scope, credit planning, and whether the finished images match the intended use.

Is Soccer good for a first request?

Yes, if the intended use is clear and the source photos are current, sharp, and permission-safe. If you are testing a dramatic change, start narrower so the first private gallery can show whether the direction deserves a larger credit spend.

How many source photos should I prepare?

Use enough images to show identity, angle, and expression without adding confusion. A small set of clear portraits usually beats a large group of old, filtered, or mixed-purpose images.

When should I choose another category instead?

Choose another category when the review criteria change. If Soccer is being judged by a different use case, style world, or motion need, split the work into a separate private job so credits support a clearer outcome.

Soccer works best when it is treated as a focused planning choice. Prepare the right inputs, review the cost, and let the private gallery show what should happen next.

settings.body: This policy explains the cookies and local storage used on www.mydreamshoots.com for the myDreamshoots AI photo service.
settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. myDreamshoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps myDreamshoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

videoThemes.name: Cinematic Portrait Motion
videoThemes.headline: A refined moving portrait with subtle camera drift.
videoThemes.description: Turns a finished portrait into a realistic short profile clip with gentle movement.
videoThemes.prompt: Create one polished realistic short professional headshot video from the supplied image frame. Preserve the visible business portrait subject, office or studio portrait setting, wardrobe color, lighting direction, face-safe broad likeness cues, and clean headshot composition while adding subtle breathing motion, natural expression, soft parallax, and a slow cinematic push-in. Do not change into a market, mountain, pet, wedding, travel, cyberpunk, or empty landscape scene. No text, logos, UI, subtitles, watermarks, split screens, or collage layouts.

videoThemes.name: Creator Intro Motion
videoThemes.headline: A compact intro clip for creator profiles and reels.
videoThemes.description: Adds polished motion to portrait photos, media-kit frames, and social intros.
videoThemes.prompt: Create one polished beauty or hairstyle intro video from the supplied salon-style portrait frame. Preserve the subject, hairstyle, wardrobe, beauty lighting, and clean profile composition while adding subtle camera travel, natural expression movement, and a confident intro-like visual rhythm. Do not turn it into a wedding couple, landscape, market, cat room, product stall, or travel scene. Keep it realistic and free of captions, logos, UI, borders, watermarks, or collage layouts.

videoThemes.name: Holiday Card Motion
videoThemes.headline: A warm seasonal clip from a finished card image.
videoThemes.description: Adds tasteful festive motion while keeping the private portrait frame stable.
videoThemes.prompt: Create one warm gala or celebration keepsake video from the supplied formal portrait frame. Preserve the visible person, formal outfit, pose, venue lighting, and card-like portrait composition while adding gentle festive atmosphere, soft light movement, and cozy cinematic camera drift. Do not output cats, window seats, mountains, markets, food stalls, empty landscapes, or unrelated characters. No text overlays, logos, UI, watermarks, or extra unrelated characters.

videoThemes.name: Product Showcase Motion
videoThemes.headline: A compact product or creator-commerce reveal.
videoThemes.description: Animates a product-style frame with controlled light and smooth camera movement.
videoThemes.prompt: Create one realistic creator-commerce or media-kit motion video from the supplied creator portrait frame. Preserve the visible creator subject, studio or desk props, microphone or camera-adjacent cues if present, wardrobe, colors, and composition while adding controlled studio light movement, soft reflections, and a smooth reveal camera move. Do not invent a produce market, food stall, shoppers, grocery baskets, labels, claims, logos, text, or unrelated product details not shown in the reference.

videoThemes.name: Prompt Directed Motion
videoThemes.headline: A neutral motion preset that follows the image and note.
videoThemes.description: Keeps the source frame as the creative lead for flexible image-to-video ideas.
videoThemes.prompt: Create one realistic cyberpunk portrait motion video from the supplied neon city portrait frame. Preserve the visible subject, action, pose, futuristic wardrobe cues, rain or neon lighting, scene facts, and lighting before adding subtle camera motion. Do not output an empty mountain lake, nature scene, market, pet room, wedding, office, or generic travel clip. No text, logos, UI, subtitles, watermarks, split screens, or collage panels.

videoThemes.name: Social Profile Clip
videoThemes.headline: A crisp clip for profile headers and creator cards.
videoThemes.description: Adds clean expression movement and editorial light for social-ready profile moments.
videoThemes.prompt: Create one clean social profile video from the supplied fan portrait frame. Keep the visible stadium or fan-photo subject realistic and confident, preserve the outfit, pose, celebratory expression, and sports-fan atmosphere, and add a controlled camera slide with natural expression movement and crisp editorial lighting. Do not turn the frame into a mountain lake, empty landscape, market, pet scene, office headshot, or wedding. Keep the output uncluttered with no text overlays, logos, borders, UI, or watermarks.

videoThemes.name: Travel Route Story

settings.question: What is myDreamshoots?
settings.answer: myDreamshoots is a private AI photo and video studio for turning approved source photos into themed portraits, group images, profile assets, seasonal cards, and short motion-ready scenes.
settings.body: You choose a package or tool, review the visible credit cost, upload photos inside your account, and review the finished work in a private gallery.|It is designed for people who want to explore a visual direction before arranging a traditional shoot or commissioning repeated edits.

settings.answer: Start by choosing a package or tool that matches the result you want, then follow the upload and generation steps shown in your signed-in workspace.
settings.body: The request flow keeps the important decisions together: source photos, package direction, selected files, credit cost, and generation status.|You can review the request before it starts, then return to the private gallery when the output is ready.
settings.bulletList: Choose a collection or tool|Upload photos you own or have permission to use|Confirm the request details and credits|Review and download finished results

settings.question: What can I create with myDreamshoots?
settings.answer: The catalog covers personal portraits, headshot, creator images, couple and group scenes, fan-inspired moments, editorial looks, seasonal cards, and selected Motion Generator.
settings.body: Different packages are organized around a visual goal, so the examples help you compare composition, wardrobe, lighting, crop, and intended channel before spending credits.
settings.bulletList: Profile and headshot|Creator and social content|Couple, friend, and group portraits|Christmas, Thanksgiving, Halloween, and seasonal albums|Short motion or video-ready add-ons

settings.question: Is myDreamshoots free?
settings.answer: Availability depends on the current tool and plan setup. Lightweight preview or utility tools may be offered without a subscription when enabled, while private model creation, premium packages, and video requests use credits.
settings.body: The request screen is the source of truth for what is available to your account and what a generation will cost.|There is no need to guess the charge: review the package, selected uploads, and credit requirement before starting.
settings.bulletList: Check the current plan and tool availability|Review credit cost before generation|Use the pricing page for current plan details

settings.question: How do plans, credits, and promotions work?
settings.answer: Plans provide account access and recurring credits, while one-time top-ups or package options can cover additional generation needs when available.
settings.body: Credit amounts, package scope, and any active promotion are shown in the current pricing or checkout experience. Promotions can change, so this FAQ intentionally does not promise a fixed bonus or duration.|Credits are tied to the account that purchased or received them and should be reviewed before a request starts.
settings.bulletList: Plans and top-ups can serve different workloads|Current pricing controls the active offer|Read checkout details before confirming payment

settings.question: When are credits used?
settings.answer: The credit requirement is shown before a request starts. Credits are reserved when generation begins, settled after successful delivery, and released when a failed request returns its reservation.
settings.body: A request may take time because image and video generation use dedicated processing capacity. The workspace keeps the request status and account history together so you can tell whether a charge was completed or released.
settings.bulletList: Review the cost before starting|Reservations can remain while a job is processing|Failed requests can release reserved credits according to status
settings.linkList: Review plan details::/pricing|Contact support about a request::/contact-us

settings.question: What photos should I upload?
settings.answer: Use recent, sharp photos where your face is visible and not heavily filtered. A small set of varied source images usually gives the workflow more useful information than many near-duplicates.
settings.body: Good source photos do not need to be professional studio images. Natural phone photos can work well when the subject is well lit, unobstructed, and captured from several useful angles.
settings.bulletList: Use clear focus and even lighting|Include front, three-quarter, and natural-expression views|Avoid sunglasses, extreme filters, heavy blur, and cropped faces|Include wardrobe or hairstyle variety when the package calls for it
settings.imageAlt: Clear source portrait showing the sharp lighting and visible face recommended for myDreamshoots AI photo uploads

settings.question: Can I create couple or group photos?
settings.answer: Yes. Couple, friend, and group results work best when every person is clearly visible in approved source photos and the chosen package is designed for more than one subject.
settings.body: For a group set, keep the source images organized and make sure each person has given permission for the intended use. Results can vary when faces are small, hidden, or heavily overlapping.
settings.bulletList: Get permission from every person shown|Use clear group and individual reference photos|Choose a package that supports the number of subjects|Review faces and hands before sharing
settings.imageAlt: myDreamshoots couple portrait showing two people in a softly lit seasonal setting for a private keepsake photo collection

settings.question: How does the AI photo generator work?
settings.answer: The generator combines your approved source photos with the selected package direction, then creates a new set of images that follows the package composition, styling, and scene cues.
settings.body: The examples show the intended visual language, but they are not a guarantee of an identical result. Source quality, pose, lighting, subject count, and model behavior all affect the finished images.
settings.bulletList: Choose a visual direction|Upload the source material|Review the request and credits|Inspect the delivered gallery and keep the strongest results
settings.imageAlt: myDreamshoots creator portrait with polished framing and social-ready styling for an AI personal-brand photo collection

settings.question: How does the AI video workflow work?
settings.answer: Selected themes can turn approved images or a prepared visual direction into short AI motion outputs. The request screen explains the supported input, expected format, and credit requirement.
settings.body: Video generation is more sensitive to image composition and motion cues than a still image request. Start with a clear hero image, keep the brief focused, and review the preview or status in your account.
settings.bulletList: Choose a video-capable theme or add-on|Use a clean source image or finished still|Confirm the duration, format, and credits shown|Download the completed motion output from the private workspace
settings.imageAlt: myDreamshoots motion-ready portrait example showing how an approved still can become a short AI video add-on

settings.question: How do virtual looks, hairstyle, and styling tools work?
settings.answer: Styling tools apply a focused visual change such as a hairstyle, virtual look, wardrobe direction, or presentation treatment while using your source photo as the starting point.
settings.body: These tools are useful when you want to compare a look before committing to a real appointment or shoot. They are visual explorations, so color, fit, texture, and facial details can vary in the generated result.
settings.bulletList: Upload a well-lit, unobstructed source image|Choose one styling direction at a time|Compare the result with the original before making decisions|Treat the output as a concept preview, not a product or fit guarantee
settings.imageAlt: myDreamshoots virtual styling portrait showing a hairstyle and outfit concept for comparing an editorial look

settings.question: Who operates myDreamshoots?
settings.answer: myDreamshoots is operated as a customer-facing AI photo studio with account, billing, generation, and gallery support handled through the site workspace.
settings.body: For a plan question, credit discrepancy, failed request, or delivery issue, include the account email, request details, and a short description so support can find the right record.|The site does not require customers to manage model providers or generation infrastructure themselves.
settings.bulletList: Use the signed-in account for request history|Keep the request or order details when contacting support|Do not send private source photos through an unrelated public channel

settings.question: Can I use AI photos on social media, profiles, or business pages?
settings.answer: You can use suitable finished images for personal profiles, social posts, creator pages, cards, campaign drafts, and other channels when you have the rights and follow the destination platform's rules.
settings.body: Before publishing, check that everyone shown has approved the use, that no protected logo or likeness is being misrepresented, and that any required AI disclosure is included.
settings.bulletList: Confirm subject and source-photo permissions|Review platform rules and disclosure requirements|Check crops, text, hands, and small details|Keep commercial claims accurate

settings.question: Are my uploads and personal data private?
settings.answer: Uploads, generation requests, albums, orders, and credit activity are associated with your signed-in account and are not public by default.
settings.body: Privacy also depends on how you share or download a result. Use the private gallery for review, avoid uploading material you do not control, and remove content when you no longer need it where the account tools allow.
settings.bulletList: Upload only material you are allowed to use|Keep account access secure|Review sharing and download choices before publishing|Read the privacy policy for retention and rights details
settings.linkList: Read the privacy policy::/privacy|Review content rules::/content

settings.question: What is the refund policy?
settings.answer: Refund eligibility follows the current refund policy, checkout terms, and the status of the specific order or generation request.
settings.body: Credits used for a successfully delivered result are generally not refundable. A failed or interrupted request may release its reservation according to the recorded status, while subscription or payment questions should be reviewed against the applicable purchase terms.
settings.bulletList: Keep the order or request reference|Check whether the generation completed or failed|Contact support promptly when a charge or delivery looks incorrect

settings.question: What can the Best AI Image page help me create?
settings.answer: The Best AI Image page helps you compare private AI image directions such as profile photos, professional portraits, creator images, seasonal albums, fashion concepts, beauty previews, product lifestyle shots, and social-ready visuals generated from approved source photos.

settings.question: How do I choose the best AI image theme for my use case?
settings.answer: Choose by destination and intent. LinkedIn headshots need a cleaner professional look, creator campaigns need expressive crops, seasonal cards need clear holiday context, and business or product images need realistic framing that matches the channel where the image will appear.

settings.question: Which source photos produce the best AI image results?
settings.answer: Use sharp, recent, well-lit photos with visible faces or subjects, natural skin detail, and minimal obstruction. Avoid heavy filters, screenshots, low-resolution crops, copyrighted references, and images of people who have not approved the intended use.

settings.question: Are AI image results private by default?
settings.answer: Generated image requests are tied to the signed-in myDreamshoots account and delivered through the private workspace or gallery. The images are not treated as a public portfolio by default, but privacy also depends on what you choose to download and share.

settings.question: Can I use generated AI images on profiles, social media, or business pages?
settings.answer: You can use suitable results when you control the source material, have permission from every person shown, follow platform rules, and include any required AI disclosure. Review commercial claims, endorsements, logos, and sensitive contexts before publishing.

settings.question: How should I review final AI images before download?
settings.answer: Check face identity, hands, teeth, eyes, text-like marks, background artifacts, clothing details, brand marks, and crop quality. Keep the strongest outputs and avoid using images that could misrepresent a person, location, product, or affiliation.

settings.question: Which still image works best for AI video generation?
settings.answer: Use a clean frame with a clear subject, balanced composition, visible face or product detail, and enough background space for movement. Avoid crowded group photos, tiny faces, heavy blur, text-heavy graphics, and images with complicated hands or overlapping objects.

settings.title: Cookie policy

settings.body: This policy explains the cookies and local storage used on www.mydreamshoots.com for the myDreamshoots AI photo service.
settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. myDreamshoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps myDreamshoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, myDreamshoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with cookie or tracking questions.

settings.question: Should I send private source photos through email or chat?
settings.answer: Avoid sending unnecessary private photos through external channels. The workspace is the preferred place for source photos and private generation records; support usually needs identifiers and a description before any additional image reference.

settings.answer: Only upload photos you own or have permission to use, and make sure every person shown has approved the intended use. Avoid misleading endorsements, protected logos, public-figure likeness issues, sensitive contexts, or content that violates the Content Policy.

seo.title: myDreamshoots KIDS Act
seo.description: Read the myDreamshoots children's privacy notice for COPPA-aware account access, minor image uploads, parent or guardian requests, and private gallery handling.

settings.body:
1. Service audience

myDreamshoots is not directed to children under 13 and is not designed for child account creation. Customers should use the service only if they can lawfully manage an account or have permission from a parent or legal guardian.

2. COPPA-aware handling

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. myDreamshoots does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. DPDPA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our DPDPA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

6. Contact

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for children's privacy or COPPA-related questions.

settings.body:

Customers may upload only photos, reference images, prompts, logos, or creative direction they own or have permission to use. Private photo packages should be based on lawful, consented source material.

Do not upload or request content involving minors, non-consenting people, stolen images, public figures, celebrities, athletes, official marks, trademarks, or protected brand assets without permission. Do not use myDreamshoots for impersonation, harassment, deception, exploitation, fake evidence, or unlawful activity.

The current policy describes how inputs are handled for service delivery; confirm the live Privacy Policy and provider terms before relying on a retention or training assumption.

Private uploads and account records are handled through signed-in account workflows; review current provider and security documentation for applicable safeguards.

myDreamshoots may review, reject, remove, rerun, or limit requests that appear unsafe, unauthorized, misleading, infringing, exploitative, or outside supported personal, creator, or business workflows.

7. Responsible output use

AI outputs can contain artifacts or inaccurate details. Review results before posting, selling, printing, or using them for profiles, campaigns, documents, or social platforms. You remain responsible for following rights, disclosure, and platform rules.

8. Reporting concerns

Email support@mydreamshoots.com with the account email, page, package, job, or gallery details if content should be reviewed or removed.

seo.description: Review how myDreamshoots handles refund review, unused credits, subscription cancellations, technical failures, reruns, billing reversals, and account credit history.

settings.body:
1. Refund review

If the shoot does not look like you, contact support for a refund review. Include your account email, order details, package name, job or gallery link, and a short explanation of the mismatch. Eligible requests may receive a refund, credit return, or rerun depending on the account history and affected generation.

2. Refund eligibility

You may request a refund for purchased credits if none of the credits from that purchase have been used. Credits spent on successful generations are generally not refundable unless myDreamshoots confirms a service-side issue or approves the refund review.

3. Failed jobs and technical issues

If a technical failure on our side prevents credit use or delivery, support may release reserved credits, rerun the job, troubleshoot the account, or approve a refund after review.

4. Trust commitments

  • Photo-use terms. The current policy describes how inputs are handled for service delivery; confirm the live Privacy Policy and provider terms before relying on a retention or training assumption.
  • Input-photo retention. Input-photo deletion follows the current retention process described in the Privacy Policy; confirm the applicable window before relying on it.
  • Secure account workflow. Uploads, requests, credit review, and galleries stay inside signed-in account workflows.
  • Refund review. If the shoot does not look like you, request a refund review.

5. Refund window and subscriptions

Refund requests should be submitted within 30 days of the purchase date. If a subscription is canceled, the customer keeps access to purchased credits until they are used or expire according to plan rules. Cancellation does not automatically refund credits already used.

6. Credit history and contact

Refunds and billing reversals appear in the customer's credit history. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with your account email and purchase details.

settings.question: What photos should I upload?
settings.answer: Use recent, sharp photos where your face is visible and not heavily filtered. A small set of varied source images usually gives the workflow more useful information than many near-duplicates.
settings.body: Good source photos do not need to be professional studio images. Natural phone photos can work well when the subject is well lit, unobstructed, and captured from several useful angles.
settings.bulletList: Use clear focus and even lighting|Include front, three-quarter, and natural-expression views|Avoid sunglasses, extreme filters, heavy blur, and cropped faces|Include wardrobe or hairstyle variety when the package calls for it

settings.answer: Choose by destination and intent. LinkedIn headshots need a cleaner professional look, creator campaigns need expressive crops, seasonal cards need clear holiday context, and business or product images need realistic framing that matches the channel where the image will appear.

settings.question: Which source photos produce the best AI image results?
settings.answer: Use sharp, recent, well-lit photos with visible faces or subjects, natural skin detail, and minimal obstruction. Avoid heavy filters, screenshots, low-resolution crops, copyrighted references, and images of people who have not approved the intended use.

settings.question: Can I use generated AI images on profiles, social media, or business pages?

settings.question: How should I review final AI images before download?
settings.answer: Check face identity, hands, teeth, eyes, text-like marks, background artifacts, clothing details, brand marks, and crop quality. Keep the strongest outputs and avoid using images that could misrepresent a person, location, product, or affiliation.

The Soccer package category helps myDreamshoots customers choose a clear package direction before they spend credits.

When Soccer is the right fit

Use Soccer when Soccer and Sports are the nearest match for the next photo set. If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest soccer requests keep the brief and the result aligned. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare clear approved source portraits, then add one cue that belongs to Soccer: light, scene texture, outfit tone, occasion, group size, or card-ready crop. Start with sharp source photos and one style cue that matters most to the package. Treat the source photos as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, fan details, holiday cues, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. myDreamshoots can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

How to compare Soccer with nearby choices

Compare soccer against neighboring packages by the job it solves, not by which cover image looks strongest. The table below turns the category into a practical choice before credit cost is confirmed.

Decision pointUse Soccer whenReview after generation
Final useUse Soccer when Sports is the right broad direction and the private album needs the specific look, scene, or keepsake format described by Soccer.Review whether the finished images look like Soccer instead of drifting into a generic Sports album.
source photosPrepare clear approved source portraits, then add one cue that belongs to Soccer: light, scene texture, outfit tone, occasion, group size, or card-ready crop.Check whether the clearest input details carried through the best images.
Category examplesSoccer and SportsKeep the outputs that match the chosen example instead of mixing several directions.
Credit planUse a focused first pass when the style is new.Decide whether the next request should repeat, expand, or change direction.

Credit and private gallery planning

Before the job starts, review the visible credit cost and ask whether the category is carrying the right amount of work. If you only need to test soccer, a smaller request can teach you what works. If the final use is already clear, a broader gallery may be easier to judge because it gives more crops and expressions to compare.

Finished outputs belong in the signed-in private gallery first. Use that space to compare identity, crop, expression, background detail, and whether the package category actually delivered the mood you selected. Download favorites only after separating public-use images from experiments.

Details to review before download

Review whether the finished images look like Soccer instead of drifting into a generic Sports album. Also check small visual details that often decide whether a result is ready for a profile, card, post, or archive: face consistency, hand and hair edges, clothing lines, background distractions, and whether the image still reads well at the crop size where you will use it.

Soccer should be recognizable through visible details such as color, posture, card framing, scene texture, seasonal cues, supporter energy, or private keepsake mood. This is where Soccer becomes more than a menu label. The visible mood should explain why the category was chosen, while the private gallery keeps the customer in control of what stays personal and what becomes a downloaded favorite.

Mistakes to avoid

Avoid asking Soccer to cover several unrelated fan, game-day, premiere, or holiday scenes at once; the narrower theme should make review easier. The fastest way to weaken soccer results is to overload the request with unrelated goals. Do not ask one job to be a professional portrait, a themed album, a restoration pass, and a motion concept at the same time. Keep the category honest, then run a second request when the next direction is different enough to need its own review.

A planning pass before you spend credits

  • Name the exact use for the finished images.
  • Choose the clearest source photos before adding style references.
  • Match the request to Soccer and Sports, not every nearby category.
  • Review credit cost before generation starts.
  • Use the private gallery to compare results before downloading favorites.

Start with Headshot Photo Package, then compare Soccer with nearby categories before generating. The best choice is the one that makes the review criteria obvious before the first image is generated.

Soccer FAQ

Soccer questions usually come down to source quality, scope, credit planning, and whether the finished images match the intended use.

Is Soccer good for a first request?

Yes, if the intended use is clear and the source photos are current, sharp, and permission-safe. If you are testing a dramatic change, start narrower so the first private gallery can show whether the direction deserves a larger credit spend.

How many source photos should I prepare?

Use enough images to show identity, angle, and expression without adding confusion. A small set of clear portraits usually beats a large group of old, filtered, or mixed-purpose images.

When should I choose another category instead?

Choose another category when the review criteria change. If Soccer is being judged by a different use case, style world, or motion need, split the work into a separate private job so credits support a clearer outcome.

Soccer works best when it is treated as a focused planning choice. Prepare the right inputs, review the cost, and let the private gallery show what should happen next.

settings.body: This policy explains the cookies and local storage used on www.mydreamshoots.com for the myDreamshoots AI photo service.
settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. myDreamshoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps myDreamshoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, myDreamshoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with cookie or tracking questions.

settings.body:
1. Service audience

myDreamshoots is not directed to children under 13 and is not designed for child account creation. Customers should use the service only if they can lawfully manage an account or have permission from a parent or legal guardian.

2. COPPA-aware handling

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. myDreamshoots does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. DPDPA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our DPDPA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

6. Contact

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for children's privacy or COPPA-related questions.

settings.body:
1. Scope of this policy

This Privacy Policy explains how myDreamshoots handles customer accounts, uploaded source photos, generated portraits, prompts, credit activity, checkout records, cookies, support messages, and private album access.

2. Photo-use terms

Your uploaded photos, prompts, and generated private results are handled to provide the requested service. Review the live Privacy Policy and provider terms for the current data-use boundaries.

3. Input-photo retention

Input-photo deletion follows the current retention process described in the Privacy Policy; confirm the applicable window before relying on it. Generated results, billing records, security logs, dispute records, and support messages may be retained where needed for account access, legal compliance, fraud prevention, refunds, and customer support.

4. Secure account workflow

myDreamshoots protects private uploads and account data through signed-in account access, scoped sessions, security cookies, monitoring, provider controls, and storage workflows. Access checks, scoped sessions, security cookies, monitoring, and provider controls reduce unauthorized access.

5. Payments, credits, and service providers

Payments may be processed by Stripe or another connected provider. Hosting, storage, email, moderation, analytics, payment, and AI infrastructure providers may process limited data only to run, secure, generate, store, or deliver the requested service.

6. Compliance references

Our footer links include KIDS Act and DPDPA notices because privacy, child-related requests, deletion, access, correction, and regional privacy rights matter for AI photo services.

7. Your choices and contact

You may ask for access, correction, export, deletion, or help with account privacy. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with your account email and request details. We may verify account ownership before acting on sensitive requests.
settings.title: Privacy policy

settings.body:
1. Refund review

If the shoot does not look like you, contact support for a refund review. Include your account email, order details, package name, job or gallery link, and a short explanation of the mismatch. Eligible requests may receive a refund, credit return, or rerun depending on the account history and affected generation.

2. Refund eligibility

You may request a refund for purchased credits if none of the credits from that purchase have been used. Credits spent on successful generations are generally not refundable unless myDreamshoots confirms a service-side issue or approves the refund review.

3. Failed jobs and technical issues

If a technical failure on our side prevents credit use or delivery, support may release reserved credits, rerun the job, troubleshoot the account, or approve a refund after review.

4. Trust commitments

  • Photo-use terms. The current policy describes how inputs are handled for service delivery; confirm the live Privacy Policy and provider terms before relying on a retention or training assumption.
  • Input-photo retention. Input-photo deletion follows the current retention process described in the Privacy Policy; confirm the applicable window before relying on it.
  • Secure account workflow. Uploads, requests, credit review, and galleries stay inside signed-in account workflows.
  • Refund review. If the shoot does not look like you, request a refund review.

5. Refund window and subscriptions

Refund requests should be submitted within 30 days of the purchase date. If a subscription is canceled, the customer keeps access to purchased credits until they are used or expire according to plan rules. Cancellation does not automatically refund credits already used.

6. Credit history and contact

Refunds and billing reversals appear in the customer's credit history. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with your account email and purchase details.

settings.body:
No physical shipping

myDreamshoots sells digital AI photo credits, generated image packages, downloads, and private gallery access. We do not ship physical products, printed photos, USB drives, or mailed merchandise from this storefront.

Digital delivery

Credits are added after payment confirmation. Generated images are delivered inside the signed-in customer workspace or private gallery when a job completes. Delivery timing can vary based on source photo quality, selected package settings, provider availability, moderation review, and system load.

Failed or delayed jobs

If a service-side issue prevents delivery, support may release reserved credits, rerun the job, troubleshoot the account, or review refund eligibility under the refund policy.

No carrier tracking or customs

Because orders are digital, customers do not receive carrier tracking numbers and are not charged shipping, customs, duties, or physical handling fees by myDreamshoots.

Contact

Email support@mydreamshoots.com with the account email, order or job details, and a short description if a digital delivery does not appear in the workspace.

settings.question: How do I choose a myDreamshoots plan for AI photo generation?
settings.answer: Choose a plan by the number of private AI photo sets you expect to create each month. A light plan can fit occasional AI headshots or profile photos, while higher-credit plans are better for portrait photos, seasonal albums, product lifestyle images, fan photos, and Motion Generator that need more generation attempts.

settings.question: What are credits and when are they charged?
settings.answer: Credits are the account balance used for paid AI generation. myDreamshoots shows the credit cost before a package, AI headshot generator, image editing tool, or video workflow starts; credits are reserved during processing and settled only according to the recorded request status.

settings.question: Can I buy extra credits without changing my subscription?
settings.answer: When one-time top-ups are available, they add extra generation capacity to the same private customer account without replacing the active plan. The checkout screen shows the current top-up amount, credit quantity, currency, and payment terms before purchase.

settings.question: Does pricing include private galleries and downloads?

settings.question: What happens if a paid AI generation fails?
settings.answer: If a provider request fails or is interrupted before delivery, the platform records the job status and can release reserved credits according to that status. Keep the order, credit, or job reference when contacting support about a failed generation, duplicate charge, or missing gallery result.

settings.question: Which AI photo tool should I start with?
settings.answer: Start with the tool that matches the final asset you need. Use headshot tools for LinkedIn, resumes, founder bios, and team pages; creator portrait tools for media kits and campaign images; edit tools for cleanup or enhancement; and AI video tools when you want a short motion concept from an approved still image.

settings.question: What source photos work best for AI Video Generation?
settings.answer: Use sharp, recent, well-lit photos where the subject is visible and the intended edit is clear. Avoid screenshots, heavy beauty filters, tiny crops, sunglasses, blurred faces, extreme compression, and any photo you do not own or have permission to process.

settings.question: Can tool results be used for social media or business pages?

settings.question: What should I inspect before downloading or publishing results?

settings.question: Which source photos help a tool perform well?
settings.answer: Use clear, recent, well-lit photos or references you own or have permission to process. A strong upload usually shows the subject, face, product, outfit, or scene without heavy filters, tiny crops, screenshots, blur, sunglasses, or confusing background clutter.

settings.question: How do prompts and settings affect tool results?
settings.answer: Short, specific direction works better than vague requests. Mention the intended channel, crop, mood, background, outfit, or motion goal when the tool supports it, then avoid requests involving unauthorized people, protected logos, official marks, or misleading affiliations.

settings.question: How are credits handled for paid tool requests?
settings.answer: Supported tools show the credit requirement before generation starts. Credits can be reserved while the request runs, then settled or released according to the recorded job status, so customers can compare tools before starting a paid request.

settings.question: Where do generated tool results appear?
settings.answer: Finished images or clips stay connected to the signed-in myDreamshoots workspace or private gallery for review, download, and account history. Results are not public by default, but customers still control anything they download or share outside the workspace.

settings.question: What quality checks matter before publishing?
settings.answer: Review face consistency, hands, eyes, teeth, text-like marks, logos, background artifacts, crop quality, and any motion issues before using outputs on LinkedIn, creator profiles, websites, ads, printed material, or social media.

settings.question: What photos should I upload?
settings.answer: Use recent, sharp photos where your face is visible and not heavily filtered. A small set of varied source images usually gives the workflow more useful information than many near-duplicates.

settings.body:
The AI Video Add-ons package category helps myDreamshoots customers choose a clear package direction before they spend credits.

When AI Video Add-ons is the right fit

Use AI Video Add-ons when AI Video Add-ons and Video are the nearest match for the next photo set. If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest ai motion generator requests keep the brief and the result aligned. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare clear approved source portraits, then add one cue that belongs to AI Video Add-ons: light, scene texture, outfit tone, occasion, group size, or card-ready crop. Start with sharp source photos and one style cue that matters most to the package. Treat the source photos as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, fan details, holiday cues, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. myDreamshoots can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

How to compare AI Video Add-ons with nearby choices

Compare ai motion generator against neighboring packages by the job it solves, not by which cover image looks strongest. The table below turns the category into a practical choice before credit cost is confirmed.

Credit and private gallery planning

Before the job starts, review the visible credit cost and ask whether the category is carrying the right amount of work. If you only need to test ai motion generator, a smaller request can teach you what works. If the final use is already clear, a broader gallery may be easier to judge because it gives more crops and expressions to compare.

Finished outputs belong in the signed-in private gallery first. Use that space to compare identity, crop, expression, background detail, and whether the package category actually delivered the mood you selected. Download favorites only after separating public-use images from experiments.

Details to review before download

Review whether the finished images look like AI Video Add-ons instead of drifting into a generic Video album. Also check small visual details that often decide whether a result is ready for a profile, card, post, or archive: face consistency, hand and hair edges, clothing lines, background distractions, and whether the image still reads well at the crop size where you will use it.

AI Video Add-ons should be recognizable through visible details such as color, posture, card framing, scene texture, seasonal cues, supporter energy, or private keepsake mood. This is where AI Video Add-ons becomes more than a menu label. The visible mood should explain why the category was chosen, while the private gallery keeps the customer in control of what stays personal and what becomes a downloaded favorite.

Mistakes to avoid

Avoid asking AI Video Add-ons to cover several unrelated fan, game-day, premiere, or holiday scenes at once; the narrower theme should make review easier. The fastest way to weaken ai motion generator results is to overload the request with unrelated goals. Do not ask one job to be a professional portrait, a themed album, a restoration pass, and a motion concept at the same time. Keep the category honest, then run a second request when the next direction is different enough to need its own review.

A planning pass before you spend credits

  • Name the exact use for the finished images.
  • Choose the clearest source photos before adding style references.
  • Match the request to AI Video Add-ons and Video, not every nearby category.
  • Review credit cost before generation starts.
  • Use the private gallery to compare results before downloading favorites.

Start with Headshot Photo Package, then compare AI Video Add-ons with nearby categories before generating. The best choice is the one that makes the review criteria obvious before the first image is generated.

AI Video Add-ons FAQ

AI Video Add-ons questions usually come down to source quality, scope, credit planning, and whether the finished images match the intended use.

Is AI Video Add-ons good for a first request?

Yes, if the intended use is clear and the source photos are current, sharp, and permission-safe. If you are testing a dramatic change, start narrower so the first private gallery can show whether the direction deserves a larger credit spend.

How many source photos should I prepare?

  • Choose the clearest source photos before adding style references.
  • Match the request to Soccer and Sports, not every nearby category.
  • Review credit cost before generation starts.
  • Use the private gallery to compare results before downloading favorites.

Start with Headshot Photo Package, then compare Soccer with nearby categories before generating. The best choice is the one that makes the review criteria obvious before the first image is generated.

Soccer FAQ

Soccer questions usually come down to source quality, scope, credit planning, and whether the finished images match the intended use.

Is Soccer good for a first request?

Yes, if the intended use is clear and the source photos are current, sharp, and permission-safe. If you are testing a dramatic change, start narrower so the first private gallery can show whether the direction deserves a larger credit spend.

How many source photos should I prepare?

Use enough images to show identity, angle, and expression without adding confusion. A small set of clear portraits usually beats a large group of old, filtered, or mixed-purpose images.

When should I choose another category instead?

Choose another category when the review criteria change. If Soccer is being judged by a different use case, style world, or motion need, split the work into a separate private job so credits support a clearer outcome.

Soccer works best when it is treated as a focused planning choice. Prepare the right inputs, review the cost, and let the private gallery show what should happen next.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. myDreamshoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps myDreamshoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, myDreamshoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with cookie or tracking questions.

seo.title: myDreamshoots KIDS Act
seo.description: Read the myDreamshoots children's privacy notice for COPPA-aware account access, minor image uploads, parent or guardian requests, and private gallery handling.

settings.body:
1. Service audience

myDreamshoots is not directed to children under 13 and is not designed for child account creation. Customers should use the service only if they can lawfully manage an account or have permission from a parent or legal guardian.

2. COPPA-aware handling

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. myDreamshoots does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. DPDPA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our DPDPA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

6. Contact

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for children's privacy or COPPA-related questions.

settings.answer: The Best AI Image page helps you compare private AI image directions such as profile photos, professional portraits, creator images, seasonal albums, fashion concepts, beauty previews, product lifestyle shots, and social-ready visuals generated from approved source photos.

settings.question: How do I choose the best AI image theme for my use case?
settings.answer: Choose by destination and intent. LinkedIn headshots need a cleaner professional look, creator campaigns need expressive crops, seasonal cards need clear holiday context, and business or product images need realistic framing that matches the channel where the image will appear.

settings.question: Which source photos produce the best AI image results?
settings.answer: Use sharp, recent, well-lit photos with visible faces or subjects, natural skin detail, and minimal obstruction. Avoid heavy filters, screenshots, low-resolution crops, copyrighted references, and images of people who have not approved the intended use.

settings.question: Are AI image results private by default?
settings.answer: Generated image requests are tied to the signed-in myDreamshoots account and delivered through the private workspace or gallery. The images are not treated as a public portfolio by default, but privacy also depends on what you choose to download and share.

settings.question: Can I use generated AI images on profiles, social media, or business pages?
settings.answer: You can use suitable results when you control the source material, have permission from every person shown, follow platform rules, and include any required AI disclosure. Review commercial claims, endorsements, logos, and sensitive contexts before publishing.

settings.question: How should I review final AI images before download?
settings.answer: Check face identity, hands, teeth, eyes, text-like marks, background artifacts, clothing details, brand marks, and crop quality. Keep the strongest outputs and avoid using images that could misrepresent a person, location, product, or affiliation.

settings.question: Which still image works best for AI video generation?
settings.answer: Use a clean frame with a clear subject, balanced composition, visible face or product detail, and enough background space for movement. Avoid crowded group photos, tiny faces, heavy blur, text-heavy graphics, and images with complicated hands or overlapping objects.

settings.body:
The Soccer package category helps myDreamshoots customers choose a clear package direction before they spend credits.

When Soccer is the right fit

Use Soccer when Soccer and Sports are the nearest match for the next photo set. If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest soccer requests keep the brief and the result aligned. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare clear approved source portraits, then add one cue that belongs to Soccer: light, scene texture, outfit tone, occasion, group size, or card-ready crop. Start with sharp source photos and one style cue that matters most to the package. Treat the source photos as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, fan details, holiday cues, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. myDreamshoots can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

How to compare Soccer with nearby choices

Compare soccer against neighboring packages by the job it solves, not by which cover image looks strongest. The table below turns the category into a practical choice before credit cost is confirmed.

Decision pointUse Soccer whenReview after generation
Final useUse Soccer when Sports is the right broad direction and the private album needs the specific look, scene, or keepsake format described by Soccer.Review whether the finished images look like Soccer instead of drifting into a generic Sports album.
source photosPrepare clear approved source portraits, then add one cue that belongs to Soccer: light, scene texture, outfit tone, occasion, group size, or card-ready crop.Check whether the clearest input details carried through the best images.
Category examplesSoccer and SportsKeep the outputs that match the chosen example instead of mixing several directions.
Credit planUse a focused first pass when the style is new.Decide whether the next request should repeat, expand, or change direction.

Credit and private gallery planning

Before the job starts, review the visible credit cost and ask whether the category is carrying the right amount of work. If you only need to test soccer, a smaller request can teach you what works. If the final use is already clear, a broader gallery may be easier to judge because it gives more crops and expressions to compare.

Finished outputs belong in the signed-in private gallery first. Use that space to compare identity, crop, expression, background detail, and whether the package category actually delivered the mood you selected. Download favorites only after separating public-use images from experiments.

Details to review before download

Review whether the finished images look like Soccer instead of drifting into a generic Sports album. Also check small visual details that often decide whether a result is ready for a profile, card, post, or archive: face consistency, hand and hair edges, clothing lines, background distractions, and whether the image still reads well at the crop size where you will use it.

Soccer should be recognizable through visible details such as color, posture, card framing, scene texture, seasonal cues, supporter energy, or private keepsake mood. This is where Soccer becomes more than a menu label. The visible mood should explain why the category was chosen, while the private gallery keeps the customer in control of what stays personal and what becomes a downloaded favorite.

Mistakes to avoid

Avoid asking Soccer to cover several unrelated fan, game-day, premiere, or holiday scenes at once; the narrower theme should make review easier. The fastest way to weaken soccer results is to overload the request with unrelated goals. Do not ask one job to be a professional portrait, a themed album, a restoration pass, and a motion concept at the same time. Keep the category honest, then run a second request when the next direction is different enough to need its own review.

A planning pass before you spend credits

  • Name the exact use for the finished images.
  • Choose the clearest source photos before adding style references.
  • Match the request to Soccer and Sports, not every nearby category.
  • Review credit cost before generation starts.
  • Use the private gallery to compare results before downloading favorites.

Start with Headshot Photo Package, then compare Soccer with nearby categories before generating. The best choice is the one that makes the review criteria obvious before the first image is generated.

Soccer FAQ

Soccer questions usually come down to source quality, scope, credit planning, and whether the finished images match the intended use.

Is Soccer good for a first request?

Yes, if the intended use is clear and the source photos are current, sharp, and permission-safe. If you are testing a dramatic change, start narrower so the first private gallery can show whether the direction deserves a larger credit spend.

How many source photos should I prepare?

Use enough images to show identity, angle, and expression without adding confusion. A small set of clear portraits usually beats a large group of old, filtered, or mixed-purpose images.

When should I choose another category instead?

Choose another category when the review criteria change. If Soccer is being judged by a different use case, style world, or motion need, split the work into a separate private job so credits support a clearer outcome.

Soccer works best when it is treated as a focused planning choice. Prepare the right inputs, review the cost, and let the private gallery show what should happen next.

settings.body: This policy explains the cookies and local storage used on www.mydreamshoots.com for the myDreamshoots AI photo service.
settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. myDreamshoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps myDreamshoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, myDreamshoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with cookie or tracking questions.

1. Service audience

myDreamshoots is not directed to children under 13 and is not designed for child account creation. Customers should use the service only if they can lawfully manage an account or have permission from a parent or legal guardian.

2. COPPA-aware handling

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. myDreamshoots does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. DPDPA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our DPDPA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

6. Contact
