Separate editorial, try-on, creator, and product work

Fashion Editorial builds a visual story around styling. Virtual Try-On explores an outfit on a person but cannot prove exact fit. Creator Portraits prioritizes personal-brand reuse. Product Style centers the merchandise and packaging rather than the model's editorial narrative.

Inspect construction before judging mood

  • Trace necklines, lapels, sleeves, hems, straps, and closures from frame to frame.
  • Inspect fingers, feet, crossed limbs, jewelry attachments, and fabric intersections.
  • Confirm that the same garment does not change length, pattern, or material without intention.
  • Check mirrors, shadows, furniture, runway edges, and repeated background figures.
  • Remove invented magazine mastheads, designer marks, care labels, and product text.
  • Review the sequence as a whole for palette, model identity, and narrative continuity.

Treat the output as a concept until production clears it

Secure model permission and review commercial rights for garments, trademarks, artwork, locations, and referenced photography. Do not claim a concept appeared in a publication or campaign when it did not. For a real product launch, confirm the physical item through conventional product and fitting photography, and disclose material AI editing where the market or publisher requires it.

AI fashion editorial FAQ

Can these images replace a product lookbook?

Use them for concepts and previsualization unless the physical garment has been checked independently. Generated construction, fit, color, and texture may differ from the product.

Can I name a designer in the brief?

Describe the design attributes you need and use only marks or protected trade dress you are authorized to use. A brand reference does not grant campaign rights.

How do I keep clothing consistent across frames?

Define construction details in writing, reuse a small reference set, and reject frames where seams, layers, patterns, or accessories change without editorial intent.

Use Magic Upscaler when a valuable photo is soft, dark, compressed, or too small for its intended display. In myDreamshoots, this workflow is available through the Photo Enhancer package. Start with the cleanest available original

Choose the original camera file or highest-quality export you can find. A screenshot, messaging-app copy, or social-media download may already contain compression, resizing, and sharpening artifacts. Enhancement can make those defects more visible. Keep an untouched copy so every result can be compared against the same source.

Check that the face or subject still contains real edges and tonal variation. Crop only when the final use requires it. If the image is severely blurred, physically damaged, or already sharp but needs portrait cleanup, another tool may match the defect more closely.

Understand what enhancement cannot recover

Enhancement can improve perceived clarity and readability, but it cannot guarantee recovery of detail that is absent from the source. Newly sharpened facial features, text, jewelry, hair, fabric, and background patterns may be generated interpretation. Compare them with the original instead of assuming that every crisp edge is historically or physically accurate.

Use the result as an enhanced version for review, not as proof that missing source detail was recovered exactly.

ToolUse it whenReview closely
Photo EnhancerGeneral clarity, brightness, and download quality need improvement.Overall sharpness, tone, noise, and natural texture.

Compare the result at 100 percent and normal size

Inspect at 100 percent to find local artifacts, then return to the normal display size to judge whether the image actually looks better. Excess sharpening can seem impressive while zoomed in but create harsh skin, glowing edges, or noisy backgrounds in normal use.

  • Compare skin texture, eyelashes, teeth, hair strands, and expression.
  • Inspect text, jewelry, straight edges, and repeating background patterns.
  • Look for ringing halos, false texture, oversharpened noise, and color shifts.
  • Confirm that identity and facial proportions did not change.
  • Review the exact crop and display size where the file will be used.

Keep the original and record the intended use

Do not overwrite the only source file. Store the original beside the enhanced version and name the intended use, such as profile crop, larger display, personal archive, or cleaner download. If factual detail matters, treat the original as the reference and the enhanced file as an edited derivative.

Photo enhancement FAQ

When is a photo suitable for enhancement?

A photo is a reasonable candidate when the subject remains identifiable and real edges or tonal detail are still present. A severely damaged or missing subject may require restoration rather than general enhancement.

Should I upload the original or a social-media copy?

Upload the highest-quality original available. Social copies and screenshots often contain compression artifacts that become more visible after sharpening.

What details should I compare afterward?

Compare identity, skin, hair, eyes, teeth, text, straight edges, repeating textures, noise, and halos. Keep the original open during review so new detail is not mistaken for recovered fact.

Choose Travel when coast, mountain, resort, or route-story scenery should shape the image. Start with the publishing destination so the scene and crop serve a real use.

Name the publishing channel before choosing a scene

Decide whether the image is for a profile avatar, vertical story, feed portrait, newsletter header, landing-page hero, or campaign draft. A square avatar needs immediate face recognition and a quiet background. A vertical story needs body framing that survives interface overlays. A header needs width and safe negative space for approved copy.

Choose whether the final frame needs face-forward impact, full-body context, or room for text. This decision belongs before generation because a visually strong portrait can still fail when the subject is covered by navigation, captions, or platform controls.

Choose Urban or Travel based on the main promise

DirectionScene languageCreator use
UrbanCity street, rooftop, subway, alley, and contemporary architectureModern profiles, editorial posts, streetwear, and city-led campaigns.
TravelCoast, mountain route, resort, old city, and scenic locationDestination-style stories, lifestyle headers, and scenic personal-brand concepts.
Nature guideForest, mountain, lake, or meadow where landscape leadsOutdoor portraits whose environment matters more than a campaign format.

Use the live Urban or Travel product card to review current outputs and credit cost. The guide does not copy those changing values.

Prepare source photos and remove unapproved brand claims

Use current portraits with the expression and body framing required by the destination channel. Choose one setting and simple wardrobe that separates clearly from the background. Remove unlicensed logos, venue marks, product labels, or campaign claims from references unless you have permission to use them.

Do not imply that a generated scene documents a real trip, venue booking, brand partnership, or city endorsement. Signs, landmarks, products, and background text need review before publication. Follow the destination platform's AI disclosure rules when material edits must be identified.

Review the image at its real publishing size

  • Check face and hand detail at the final crop size.
  • Review subject-to-background scale, perspective, horizon, and shadows.
  • Inspect hair edges, repeated architecture, foliage, signs, and logos.
  • Confirm there is safe space for copy without covering the subject.
  • Preview the image behind expected interface overlays.
  • Check that a generated location or partnership is not implied as real.

Add verified text after generation

Generate a clean scene first. Add headlines, dates, calls to action, and campaign copy later in a design tool where spelling and placement can be controlled. This also separates the visual concept from factual or commercial claims that require approval.

Outdoor creator FAQ

Is Outdoor Creator Scenes a separate product?

No. Use this page to decide between Urban and Travel based on whether a city or scenic location better supports the final creator use.

Which direction works for a profile avatar?

Either can work if the face remains legible at square size. Choose the scene whose background stays quiet enough to support recognition rather than competing with it.

Can I describe the scene as a real trip or partnership?

Do not make that claim from a generated image. Use real evidence for travel, venue, or partnership statements and disclose material AI edits where required.

What should I preview before publishing?

Preview the final crop, interface overlays, text-safe space, face and hands, background signs, logos, landmarks, perspective, and any detail that could imply a real endorsement.

Define whether the asset is a concept or a product record

A moodboard can explore light, props, color, and audience context. A campaign draft can test composition and copy space. A final ecommerce packshot has a different burden: the product shape, quantity, color, packaging, and included components must match what buyers receive. Do not let a concept silently become a factual product image.

AssetUseful AI roleRequired verification
Lifestyle moodboardExplore setting, palette, and prop directionBrand fit and scene plausibility
Campaign draftTest hero composition and text-safe spaceProduct silhouette, claim placement, and rights
Social conceptPlan a promotional crop or launch visualPlatform crop, disclosure, and accurate offer copy
Final packshotLimited role when exactness is requiredPhysical-product photography and factual comparison

Capture the real product from several useful angles

Provide a clean front view, side or three-quarter view, and packaging reference when those surfaces matter. Record dimensions, color variant, finish, included pieces, and non-negotiable features in the brief. For reflective, transparent, flexible, or highly textured products, note how the material behaves under light.

Use only products, logos, packaging, and artwork you are authorized to depict. A competitor image may be useful for private market analysis, but copying its trade dress or publishing a confusingly similar result creates a separate rights problem.

Design the lifestyle scene around use, scale, and safety

Specify who uses the product, where, at what scale, and which props are acceptable. A bottle beside a hand, a device on a desk, or packaging in a kitchen each creates scale evidence that must be reviewed. Avoid unsafe use, impossible assembly, missing protective equipment, or a setting that implies certification or performance the product does not have.

Use the AI Image Generation directory as the CTA because a dedicated Product Style public route has not passed the required route and entity checks. This article does not send users to a semantically unrelated editor.

Separate product styling from adjacent creative work

Fashion Editorial centers garments and model-led storytelling. Social Cards centers a publishing unit that combines imagery with verified copy. Product Style keeps the item, packaging, and use context central. Conventional product photography remains the reference when exact buyer-facing representation is required.

Audit the item before admiring the scene

  • Compare overall silhouette, dimensions, openings, buttons, ports, seams, and included components.
  • Inspect logo shape, label hierarchy, variant name, quantity, and regulatory information.
  • Check color and material under highlight, shadow, reflection, and transparency.
  • Confirm scale against hands, furniture, food, tools, or other recognizable objects.
  • Remove invented awards, certifications, ingredients, performance claims, and review badges.
  • Compare the selected image side by side with the physical product or approved master photography.

Keep claims, prices, and offers outside the generated image

Add verified product names, prices, availability, dimensions, ingredients, warranties, and campaign claims in the commerce or design system. Generated text can be wrong even when it looks convincing. Legal, compliance, and brand owners should review regulated categories and commercial placements. The content policy covers prohibited deceptive and rights-infringing uses.

AI product style photo FAQ

Can I use a generated image as the main storefront packshot?

Only after strict comparison with the item buyers receive. When exact shape, color, quantity, or packaging matters, verified product photography is the safer factual reference.

Why should label text be added later?

Generated labels can invent words, quantities, ingredients, certifications, and legal copy. Use approved packaging art or add verified text in the production layout.

What if the product is only a prototype?

Label the image as a concept and avoid presenting unconfirmed features, materials, availability, or performance as final.

settings.body:
A professional AI headshot should look like a current, credible version of the subject, not a different person in formal clothing. Start with recent portraits, match wardrobe and background to the real role, keep retouching restrained, and test the final image in the LinkedIn, resume, or team-directory crop where it will appear.

Match the headshot to the professional context

LinkedIn usually rewards a recognizable face and simple shoulders-up crop. A resume or CV photo, where locally appropriate, should remain compact and neutral. Team directories benefit from consistent framing across people. Speaker and author bios can carry slightly more personality while remaining accurate to the person's current work.

PlacementRecommended directionCheck before use
LinkedInApproachable face-led square cropRecognition at small size and platform policy
Resume or CVNeutral, compact, role-appropriate portraitLocal norms and employer expectations
Team directoryConsistent light, crop, and backgroundFair treatment and permission for each person
Speaker bioPolished portrait with modest personalityCurrent identity and factual affiliation

Use current source portraits with natural detail

Select a clear image with visible eyes, hairline, jaw, and skin texture. Neutral light is easier to evaluate than strong colored light. Add another angle only when it clarifies glasses, hairstyle, or expression. Avoid old life stages, beauty-filter screenshots, group photos, face-obscuring accessories, and images where the source has already been heavily retouched.

Open the current Headshot page before starting. The portrait should be based on the person's real appearance and role, not on an invented title, uniform, badge, or workplace.

Choose credible wardrobe, light, and background

Describe the degree of formality rather than assuming every profession needs a dark suit. A creative lead, therapist, engineer, consultant, and hospitality manager may need different styling. Use a clean studio tone, restrained office suggestion, or simple environmental background. Avoid official insignia, medical or public-safety uniforms, client logos, and settings that imply employment or certification without authorization.

Compare Headshot with adjacent portrait workflows

Creator Portraits allows more expressive brand storytelling and thumbnail variation. Profile Cards builds a repeatable portrait-plus-bio system. Portrait Retouch is useful when an existing professional photograph already has the right composition and only needs controlled cleanup. Headshot is the focused choice when a new professional portrait direction is needed.

Review credibility before polish

  • Compare face shape, eye spacing, skin tone, hairline, teeth, glasses, and age with the source.
  • Look for waxy skin, erased lines, artificial teeth, and over-sharpened eyes.
  • Inspect collars, lapels, buttons, jewelry, hair edges, and eyeglass temples.
  • Check background architecture, books, screens, signage, and pseudo-logos.
  • Test square, circular, and small resume crops without cutting the chin or hair awkwardly.
  • Ask the subject to approve the final image before it enters a team or public profile.

Do not turn presentation into a false credential

A polished portrait does not prove identity, employment, licensing, education, or professional membership. Add names, titles, certifications, and company relationships from verified records in the profile system. Some employers, jurisdictions, and identity services have specific photo rules; follow those requirements and use a conventional current photograph when requested.

Professional AI headshot FAQ

Can I use an AI headshot on LinkedIn?

Use a recognizable, non-deceptive image that follows current platform and employer expectations. Do not use it to impersonate someone or invent a role.

Should a resume include a headshot?

Norms vary by country, industry, and employer. Check local guidance before adding any photo to a resume or CV.

How much retouching is appropriate?

Keep stable facial features, age, skin texture, and distinguishing details recognizable. Correct presentation issues without creating a materially different identity.

Profile card photos should make the same approved person easy to recognize across bios, directories, and social profiles. Treat profile cards as a small identity system

Inventory every destination before creating the image set. A team grid may require equal shoulder position across many people. An author bio may need a warmer expression. Create one stable identity base

Choose a recent face-forward portrait with visible eyes, hairline, and natural expression. A second angle can clarify hairstyle or glasses, but a large mixed set often introduces age, grooming, and identity conflicts. Avoid group photos, heavy filters, hats, tiny crops, and references of several different people.

Use portraits you own or have permission to edit. Team and community profiles need explicit subject approval for the intended channel, not merely access to an old photograph.

Plan crop, background, and text-safe space together

Set a repeatable head size, eye line, shoulder position, background family, and edge clearance. Test the tightest destination first. If a card needs copy beside the portrait, reserve quiet space but add the words later. Generated names, roles, credentials, dates, and contact details are not reliable profile data.

The visual workflow is available through Avatar. Review the current product page before creating the set, then use your profile or design system for the factual layer.

Distinguish Profile Cards from Avatar and Headshot pages

An illustrated character-style direction serves a different purpose from Professional Headshots, which prioritizes workplace credibility and realism. Creator Portraits builds a broader media library.   • Remove badges, labels, pseudo-text, or objects that imply a role or credential.

Keep image approval and profile data traceable

Store the approved source, selected image, subject approval, and current copy together. Update the portrait when it no longer reasonably represents the person. Do not use a profile card as identity documentation, background-check evidence, or proof of employment. Follow the destination's requirements when it asks for an unedited photograph.

Profile card photo FAQ

Is a profile card the same as an illustrated profile image?

No. A profile card is a publishing format for consistent bios and social identities. It may use a stylized image workflow, but its entity, layout rules, and factual copy requirements are different.

Should names and job titles be generated inside the portrait?

No. Add verified names, roles, links, and contact details in the card layout or content management system.

How do I keep a team grid consistent?

Document crop ratio, head size, eye line, background, wardrobe range, and approval process, then apply the same review standard to every person.

Reduce the card to one message and one action

Can the model create the final headline in the image?

Thanksgiving group photos should begin with an approved participant roster and a clear plan for a card, Friendsgiving album, family-style portrait, or gratitude post. Keep the arrangement simple enough to see every face, decide whether the table is central or only background context, and inspect hands, food, tableware, and relationships before selecting a warm-looking result.

Define the gathering without inventing attendance

List every person who should appear and confirm that they approve the source image, generated grouping, and destination. Do not add a relative, friend, public figure, or absent person to imply that they attended a gathering. A composite can be a private concept, but it should never be described as documentary evidence of a real dinner.

Choose whether the frame represents family, chosen family, friends, coworkers, or another approved group. Avoid forcing a traditional family structure or assigning relationships that the participants have not stated. If different groups need cards, create separate rosters and review them independently.

Choose table, standing group, or card portrait

A dinner-table frame creates atmosphere but adds difficult hands, plates, glasses, chairs, and overlapping bodies. A standing or seated portrait away from the table keeps faces larger. A gratitude card needs extra negative space. Pick the arrangement based on final use rather than treating a crowded table as mandatory.

ArrangementStrengthReview burden
Dinner tableStrong gathering atmosphereHands, plates, food, and face occlusion
Seated portraitClearer rows and expressionsChair geometry and body scale
Standing groupFlexible card cropHeight, spacing, and overlapping arms
Small Friendsgiving setNatural interactionAccurate roster and relationship framing

Prepare readable sources for every participant

Use recent portraits with visible eyes, hair, and natural expression. Keep quality and age reasonably consistent, and avoid tiny social screenshots or group crops where faces overlap. Label the roster outside the generation workflow so a reviewer can compare the correct source with each person in the result.

Guardian approval is required for children, and public sharing deserves a separate privacy review. Remove home addresses, school identifiers, family documents, screens, and name tags from references. Only include pets when their presence is intentional and the composition remains manageable.

Use a few gathering cues instead of a prop inventory

Warm interior light, harvest color, a restrained table setting, simple seasonal foliage, or a neutral home backdrop can establish the context. Do not overload the scene with every possible dish and decoration. The participants should remain the focal point, and the setting should leave enough space for a gratitude message when needed.

Review the current Thanksgiving Photo page before starting. Treat food, tableware, and decor as visual concepts, not accurate recipes, product claims, or evidence of a real venue.

Keep gratitude messages factual and separate

Add names, year, host information, event details, quotations, and gratitude messages after the image is selected. Generated lettering can look convincing while being wrong. Confirm that the final wording represents the group and does not reveal private information or make attendance claims.

Choose Thanksgiving only when gathering is central

Holiday Photos supports broad winter or year-end portraits without a dinner or gratitude focus. Christmas Photos centers specifically Christmas cards and festive family or friend groups. Christmas Couple is narrower still. Thanksgiving Group Photos is for an approved gathering roster, gratitude card, or table-adjacent group album.

Review the group from faces to table edges

  • Count every participant and compare each face, age, hair, expression, and body scale with the roster.
  • Check seating order, eye lines, chair placement, overlapping shoulders, and whether anyone is hidden or duplicated.
  • Trace hands, fingers, utensils, plate edges, glasses, serving dishes, tablecloth patterns, and contact with food.
  • Remove accidental writing, brand marks, unsafe candle details, distorted food, and background people.
  • Preview the selected image in the final card, square post, or album crop without cutting off participants.
  • Add and proofread the exact gratitude message, names, year, and destination information after review.

Protect family and friend privacy

Do not publish a composite in a way that misrepresents a real gathering or a person's relationships. Ask participants or guardians to approve the selected output and audience. The content policy provides additional limits for identity, misleading scenes, minors, and third-party material.

Thanksgiving group photo FAQ

Does the group need to sit at a dinner table?

No. A standing or seated portrait can preserve faces more reliably while warm light and restrained decor carry the Thanksgiving context.

Can this page be used for Friendsgiving?

Yes. Define the approved friend roster and desired tone, and avoid implying that a generated composite documents a real event.

How should I handle a large family group?

Use clear individual sources and consider smaller related frames when the full group makes faces too small or overlaps too complex to verify.

Hair, hands, bags, and jewelry can overlap fabric, so make sure those elements are readable in the source.

Use current photos you own or have permission to use. A heavily filtered face, extreme pose, cropped garment area, or deep shadow makes it harder to judge whether the preview preserved the person and placed the clothing coherently.

Use one approved clothing reference and styling direction

Add one clothing reference that you own or have permission to use. Describe one direction such as casual, formal, streetwear, travel, or event styling. Avoid combining several garments whose cut, layers, or branding compete. Protected logos and branded product images need appropriate rights before they are used or published.

Treat the output as a moodboard, not a fit guarantee

The preview may not reproduce a garment's exact size, cut, fabric weight, texture, transparency, color, pattern placement, closures, or drape. It cannot confirm comfort, inventory, tailoring, or how the physical item will fit. Check the seller's product page, size chart, materials, product photos, and return policy before making a purchase decision.

WorkflowWhat changesUse it when
Virtual Try-OnWardrobe direction on a personYou want a visual outfit concept, not a measurement.
Street StyleClothing and a complete fashion sceneThe setting matters as much as the outfit.
Portrait RetouchAn existing portrait without replacing the outfitThe source is already dressed correctly and needs controlled cleanup.
Hairstyle GeneratorHair direction rather than wardrobeThe clothing should stay secondary to a hairstyle decision.

Review the live Virtual Try-On package card for current outputs and credit cost before starting.

Review garment, body, and identity artifacts

  • Check neckline, shoulders, sleeves, cuffs, waist, hem, and closures.
  • Inspect pattern continuity, fabric edges, transparency, and repeated texture.
  • Review logos, labels, jewelry overlap, fingers, and hair over fabric.
  • Confirm body shape, pose, proportions, shadows, and skin remain believable.
  • Check that the outfit did not change identity, age, or expression.
  • Compare the preview with both the person photo and garment reference.

Avoid product and brand misrepresentation

Do not present a generated try-on as an exact image of a retailer's product, a verified brand collaboration, or proof of how a garment will fit. Disclose material AI changes when the publishing context requires it. The current local cover shows outfit planning beside a clothing rack; a verified source-reference-preview workflow asset remains required before this page is approved for publication.

Virtual Try-On FAQ

Does Virtual Try-On show exact garment fit?

No. The result is a visual planning image, not a measurement, material, color, or fit guarantee. Confirm purchase details using the physical product and seller information.

What person photo and garment reference work best?

Use a clear, simply lit portrait with enough body framing and one unobstructed clothing reference that you are authorized to use.

Can I use a retailer's product image?

Only when you have the rights or permission required for that image and use. Do not imply an official product rendering or brand partnership from a generated preview.

Use Wedding Photo for save-the-date concepts, ceremony moodboards, invitation-friendly portraits, wedding website visuals, or private keepsakes. Prepare approved photos of both people, choose one ceremony direction, and treat every result as wedding-inspired creative imagery rather than proof of a real event.

Choose the wedding use before the visual style

A save-the-date needs text-safe composition. A ceremony moodboard can explore atmosphere, clothing, floral direction, and light. An invitation portrait should leave room for verified copy. A website header needs a wide crop that survives navigation overlays. A private keepsake can favor emotion and close detail.

Choose Wedding Photo when formal couple styling, ceremony atmosphere, floral details, or card-ready framing is central. Choose Engagement for a proposal or ring-led announcement. Choose Valentine's Day for a seasonal romantic card that does not make a ceremony claim.

Prepare both people and one ceremony direction

Use recent, clear portraits of both people with similar lighting and useful face angles. Confirm that each person approves the source images, generated pairing, intended audience, and final use. Then choose one direction: ceremony, formal studio, outdoor romance, or card-ready portrait.

Include only cultural, floral, wardrobe, jewelry, and ceremonial details that knowledgeable participants can review accurately. Do not invent family traditions, religious meaning, or event facts that were not supplied.

Match the theme to the relationship claim

ThemePrimary formatBoundary
Wedding PhotoCeremony-led concepts, formal portraits, save-the-dates, and keepsakesDo not present generated imagery as event documentation.
Engagement PhotoProposal, ring, and announcement-led imageryThe announcement and relationship claim must be real and approved.
Valentine's DaySeasonal romantic cards, date-night portraits, and giftsUse seasonal language without implying a ceremony.

Add names, dates, and venue copy later

Leave names, dates, venue details, invitation copy, and schedules out of the generated scene. Add verified text later in a design tool where spelling, hierarchy, and date accuracy can be controlled. A clean text-safe crop is more reliable than generated lettering that appears correct at first glance.

Review consent, ceremony details, and pair anatomy

Use generated wedding images as concepts or keepsakes, not as proof that a ceremony, venue booking, marriage, or cultural rite occurred. Share couple images only with both people's approval.

  • Check both faces, eye direction, expression, and relative scale.
  • Inspect overlapping hands and arms, rings, jewelry, and bouquet stems.
  • Review veil and hair edges, suit and dress fabric, and floral repetition.
  • Check ceremonial objects, cultural details, background guests, and venue cues.
  • Confirm the final card or website crop preserves text-safe spacing.
  • Have knowledgeable participants review meaningful attire, symbols, and rituals.

AI wedding portrait FAQ

Can a generated wedding portrait document a real ceremony?

No. Use it as a concept, moodboard, invitation-friendly visual, or keepsake. Real event claims require real documentation.

Who should approve a couple image?

Both people should approve the source photos, generated pairing, relationship claim, intended audience, and final use.

Where should names and dates be added?

Add verified copy after generation in a design tool so spelling, dates, hierarchy, and placement can be controlled.

How should cultural details be reviewed?

Include only details supplied by the participants and ask knowledgeable people to review attire, symbols, rituals, and ceremonial objects before publication.

Choose one personal fan format

Use personal portraits or group references that you have permission to use. Pick one generic color direction and one format so the result has a clear job.

FormatCompositionReview priority
Profile avatarSquare, face-led, minimal backgroundRecognition at small size and no accidental marks.
Match-day posterVertical, energetic light, clean space for later copyHands, jersey details, stadium geometry, and text-safe area.
Social bannerWide, subject placed away from interface overlaysCrop resilience, crowd repetition, and background signs.
Supporter groupOnly approved people, with clear spacingEvery face, hand, garment, and relationship between figures.

Use generic supporter colors and invented scene details

Use generic colors, unbranded clothing, invented stadium details, and personal fan expressions. Do not include official competition names or marks, team crests, sponsor logos, player or celebrity likenesses, protected trophy designs, tickets, or branded venue assets unless you hold the required rights.

Add verified match copy later

Generate a clean poster image first. Add verified match names, dates, scores, and other copy later in a design tool. Do not rely on generated text, and do not use protected event branding without permission. If a score or date is factual, verify it independently before publishing.

Inspect every detail that could imply a real team or event

  • Check every face, hand, finger, and interaction in group scenes.
  • Inspect jersey numbers, names, stripes, seams, flags, and face paint.
  • Review balls, goal lines, crowd repetition, and stadium geometry.
  • Look for signs, sponsor-like shapes, accidental crests, and invented text.
  • Remove details that resemble a real player, tournament, team, trophy, or venue.
  • Confirm the crop works without implying official affiliation.

Keep personal fan creativity separate from commercial rights

A personal supporter image does not automatically grant rights for advertising, merchandise, ticketing, sponsorship, or commercial campaigns. Obtain the permissions required for people, marks, brands, and commercial use. Review the content policy before sharing material that may involve protected identities or branding.

Soccer fan photo FAQ

Can I request an official crest or tournament mark?

Do not include protected marks unless you hold the required rights. Use generic colors and invented supporter details for a personal fan concept.

Can the image feature a real player?

Avoid player and celebrity likenesses unless you have the necessary permission. A personal supporter portrait should focus on the approved person in the source photo.

How should poster text be handled?

Generate a clean image with text-safe space, then add verified names, dates, scores, and copy in a design tool. Keep protected event branding out unless authorized.

settings.title: Cookie policy

settings.body: This policy explains the cookies and local storage used on www.mydreamshoots.com for the myDreamshoots AI photo service.
settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. myDreamshoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps myDreamshoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, myDreamshoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with cookie or tracking questions.

settings.subtitle: Detailed help for AI photo requests, account access, billing, credits, policies, private galleries, uploads, and delivery questions.
settings.journeyDescriptions: Choose the right page path.|Use approved source photos.|Check credits before generation.|Keep results in your private gallery.

settings.question: How do I get help with an AI photo or AI video request?
settings.answer: Contact support with the account email, order reference, job reference, package or tool name, and a short description of what happened. Those details help the team locate the generation request, credit reservation, payment event, or private gallery record faster.

settings.question: What information should I include when reporting a bad result?
settings.answer: Include the page or tool you used, the package direction, the approximate request time, and what looks wrong in the output, such as identity mismatch, crop issue, missing download, image artifact, or video motion problem. Do not send extra private source photos unless support asks for a specific reference.

settings.question: Can support review credits, failed jobs, or refund questions?
settings.answer: Support can review visible checkout records, credit reservations, settled credits, released credits, failed-request states, and private delivery status tied to the signed-in account. Refund eligibility still follows the current Refund Policy, Terms of Service, and the recorded order status.

settings.question: Where can I read the rules before uploading photos?
settings.answer: Use the Privacy Policy, Content Policy, Terms of Service, Refund Policy, and Cookie Policy before uploading source photos, buying credits, or publishing outputs. These pages explain privacy, acceptable content, billing, refund, and site-use rules.

settings.question: Should I send private source photos through email or chat?
settings.answer: Avoid sending unnecessary private photos through external channels. The workspace is the preferred place for source photos and private generation records; support usually needs identifiers and a description before any additional image reference.

settings.question: What if my request involves another person, a brand, or sensitive content?
settings.answer: Only upload photos you own or have permission to use, and make sure every person shown has approved the intended use. Avoid misleading endorsements, protected logos, public-figure likeness issues, sensitive contexts, or content that violates the Content Policy.

seo.title: myDreamshoots KIDS Act
seo.description: Read the myDreamshoots children's privacy notice for COPPA-aware account access, minor image uploads, parent or guardian requests, and private gallery handling.

settings.body:
1. Service audience

myDreamshoots is not directed to children under 13 and is not designed for child account creation. Customers should use the service only if they can lawfully manage an account or have permission from a parent or legal guardian.

2. COPPA-aware handling

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. myDreamshoots does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. DPDPA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our DPDPA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

6. Contact

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for children's privacy or COPPA-related questions.

seo.title: Content Policy for myDreamshoots Uploads and AI Photo Outputs
seo.keywords: myDreamshoots policy, AI photo privacy, AI portrait terms, photo upload privacy, private AI albums, AI photo credits, photo-use policy, Input-photo retention, account and provider safeguards
seo.description: Read the myDreamshoots content policy for permitted source photos, upload rights, identity consent, moderation review, private album use, and the trust commitments that keep your photos out of model training and auto-delete inputs after 30 days.

settings.body:
1. Source photo permission

Customers may upload only photos, reference images, prompts, logos, or creative direction they own or have permission to use. Private photo packages should be based on lawful, consented source material.

2. Identity consent

Do not upload or request content involving minors, non-consenting people, stolen images, public figures, celebrities, athletes, official marks, trademarks, or protected brand assets without permission. Do not use myDreamshoots for impersonation, harassment, deception, exploitation, fake evidence, or unlawful activity.

3. Photo-use terms

The current policy describes how inputs are handled for service delivery; confirm the live Privacy Policy and provider terms before relying on a retention or training assumption.

4. Input-photo retention

Input-photo deletion follows the current retention process described in the Privacy Policy; confirm the applicable window before relying on it.

5. Secure account workflow

Private uploads and account records are handled through signed-in account workflows; review current provider and security documentation for applicable safeguards.

6. Moderation and blocked requests

myDreamshoots may review, reject, remove, rerun, or limit requests that appear unsafe, unauthorized, misleading, infringing, exploitative, or outside supported personal, creator, or business workflows.

7. Responsible output use

AI outputs can contain artifacts or inaccurate details. Review results before posting, selling, printing, or using them for profiles, campaigns, documents, or social platforms. You remain responsible for following rights, disclosure, and platform rules.

settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. myDreamshoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps myDreamshoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, myDreamshoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with cookie or tracking questions.

settings.question: How do I choose the best AI image theme for my use case?
settings.answer: Choose by destination and intent. LinkedIn headshots need a cleaner professional look, creator campaigns need expressive crops, seasonal cards need clear holiday context, and business or product images need realistic framing that matches the channel where the image will appear.

settings.question: Which source photos produce the best AI image results?
settings.answer: Use sharp, recent, well-lit photos with visible faces or subjects, natural skin detail, and minimal obstruction. Avoid heavy filters, screenshots, low-resolution crops, copyrighted references, and images of people who have not approved the intended use.

settings.question: How should I review final AI images before download?
settings.answer: Check face identity, hands, teeth, eyes, text-like marks, background artifacts, clothing details, brand marks, and crop quality. Keep the strongest outputs and avoid using images that could misrepresent a person, location, product, or affiliation.

The Soccer package category helps myDreamshoots customers choose a clear package direction before they spend credits.

When Soccer is the right fit

Use Soccer when Soccer and Sports are the nearest match for the next photo set. If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest soccer requests keep the brief and the result aligned. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare clear approved source portraits, then add one cue that belongs to Soccer: light, scene texture, outfit tone, occasion, group size, or card-ready crop. Start with sharp source photos and one style cue that matters most to the package. Treat the source photos as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, fan details, holiday cues, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. myDreamshoots can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

How to compare Soccer with nearby choices

Compare soccer against neighboring packages by the job it solves, not by which cover image looks strongest. The table below turns the category into a practical choice before credit cost is confirmed.

Decision pointUse Soccer whenReview after generation

Category examplesSoccer and SportsKeep the outputs that match the chosen example instead of mixing several directions.
Credit planUse a focused first pass when the style is new.Decide whether the next request should repeat, expand, or change direction.

Credit and private gallery planning

Before the job starts, review the visible credit cost and ask whether the category is carrying the right amount of work. If you only need to test soccer, a smaller request can teach you what works. If the final use is already clear, a broader gallery may be easier to judge because it gives more crops and expressions to compare.

Finished outputs belong in the signed-in private gallery first. Use that space to compare identity, crop, expression, background detail, and whether the package category actually delivered the mood you selected. Download favorites only after separating public-use images from experiments.

Details to review before download

Review whether the finished images look like Soccer instead of drifting into a generic Sports album. Also check small visual details that often decide whether a result is ready for a profile, card, post, or archive: face consistency, hand and hair edges, clothing lines, background distractions, and whether the image still reads well at the crop size where you will use it.

Soccer should be recognizable through visible details such as color, posture, card framing, scene texture, seasonal cues, supporter energy, or private keepsake mood. This is where Soccer becomes more than a menu label. The visible mood should explain why the category was chosen, while the private gallery keeps the customer in control of what stays personal and what becomes a downloaded favorite.

Mistakes to avoid

Avoid asking Soccer to cover several unrelated fan, game-day, premiere, or holiday scenes at once; the narrower theme should make review easier. The fastest way to weaken soccer results is to overload the request with unrelated goals. Do not ask one job to be a professional portrait, a themed album, a restoration pass, and a motion concept at the same time. Keep the category honest, then run a second request when the next direction is different enough to need its own review.

A planning pass before you spend credits

  • Name the exact use for the finished images.
  • Choose the clearest source photos before adding style references.
  • Match the request to Soccer and Sports, not every nearby category.
  • Review credit cost before generation starts.
  • Use the private gallery to compare results before downloading favorites.

Start with Headshot Photo Package, then compare Soccer with nearby categories before generating. The best choice is the one that makes the review criteria obvious before the first image is generated.

Soccer FAQ

Soccer questions usually come down to source quality, scope, credit planning, and whether the finished images match the intended use.

Is Soccer good for a first request?

Yes, if the intended use is clear and the source photos are current, sharp, and permission-safe. If you are testing a dramatic change, start narrower so the first private gallery can show whether the direction deserves a larger credit spend.

How many source photos should I prepare?

Use enough images to show identity, angle, and expression without adding confusion. A small set of clear portraits usually beats a large group of old, filtered, or mixed-purpose images.

When should I choose another category instead?

Choose another category when the review criteria change. If Soccer is being judged by a different use case, style world, or motion need, split the work into a separate private job so credits support a clearer outcome.

Soccer works best when it is treated as a focused planning choice. Prepare the right inputs, review the cost, and let the private gallery show what should happen next.

settings.body: This policy explains the cookies and local storage used on www.mydreamshoots.com for the myDreamshoots AI photo service.
settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. myDreamshoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps myDreamshoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, myDreamshoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with cookie or tracking questions.

myDreamshoots is not directed to children under 13 and is not designed for child account creation. Customers should use the service only if they can lawfully manage an account or have permission from a parent or legal guardian.

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. myDreamshoots does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. DPDPA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our DPDPA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

6. Contact

settings.question: What photos should I upload?
settings.answer: Use recent, sharp photos where your face is visible and not heavily filtered. A small set of varied source images usually gives the workflow more useful information than many near-duplicates.

settings.question: What can the Best AI Image page help me create?
settings.answer: The Best AI Image page helps you compare private AI image directions such as profile photos, professional portraits, creator images, seasonal albums, fashion concepts, beauty previews, product lifestyle shots, and social-ready visuals generated from approved source photos.

settings.question: How do I choose the best AI image theme for my use case?
settings.answer: Choose by destination and intent. LinkedIn headshots need a cleaner professional look, creator campaigns need expressive crops, seasonal cards need clear holiday context, and business or product images need realistic framing that matches the channel where the image will appear.

settings.question: Which source photos produce the best AI image results?
settings.answer: Use sharp, recent, well-lit photos with visible faces or subjects, natural skin detail, and minimal obstruction. Avoid heavy filters, screenshots, low-resolution crops, copyrighted references, and images of people who have not approved the intended use.

settings.question: Are AI image results private by default?
settings.answer: Generated image requests are tied to the signed-in myDreamshoots account and delivered through the private workspace or gallery. The images are not treated as a public portfolio by default, but privacy also depends on what you choose to download and share.

settings.question: Can I use generated AI images on profiles, social media, or business pages?
settings.answer: You can use suitable results when you control the source material, have permission from every person shown, follow platform rules, and include any required AI disclosure. Review commercial claims, endorsements, logos, and sensitive contexts before publishing.

settings.question: How should I review final AI images before download?
settings.answer: Check face identity, hands, teeth, eyes, text-like marks, background artifacts, clothing details, brand marks, and crop quality. Keep the strongest outputs and avoid using images that could misrepresent a person, location, product, or affiliation.

settings.question: How do I choose the right AI photo package collection?
settings.answer: Choose by the final use of the gallery: professional headshots, creator portraits, dating profile photos, couple scenes, fan-inspired moments, seasonal cards, hairstyle previews, fashion editorials, product lifestyle images, or AI video-ready stills. Each collection helps you compare the visual direction before spending credits.

settings.question: What source photos should I prepare before choosing a package?
settings.answer: Prepare clear, permission-safe photos with good lighting, visible faces, and a few angles or expressions. For identity-heavy packages such as AI headshots or creator portraits, a varied source set usually works better than many near-duplicate selfies.

settings.question: Are package examples exact guarantees?
settings.answer: No. Examples show the intended style, framing, lighting, and use case, but final results depend on source-photo quality, pose, crop, subject count, prompt direction, and AI model behavior. Use examples as a comparison guide, not as an identical-output promise.

settings.question: Can packages support couples, friends, teams, or groups?
settings.answer: Some collections are designed for more than one person, while others work best with a single subject. For group or couple AI photos, upload approved source photos for every person, choose a package that fits the group size, and review faces and hands carefully before sharing.

settings.question: Do package pages show credit costs and output expectations?
settings.answer: Package pages and generation screens show credit requirements before a request starts, and many packages also describe the expected output count or album direction. This helps you compare private AI photo packages before reserving credits.

settings.question: Where are finished package results delivered?
settings.answer: Finished images are delivered to the private myDreamshoots gallery or workspace tied to the signed-in account. You can review the gallery, keep the strongest outputs, download files, and decide what is appropriate to publish or reuse.

settings.title: Cookie policy

settings.body: This policy explains the cookies and local storage used on test.grownstride.com for the MydreamShoots AI photo service.
settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. MydreamShoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps MydreamShoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, MydreamShoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@test.grownstride.com with cookie or tracking questions.
settings.title: Cookie policy

settings.question: How do I get help with an AI photo or AI video request?
settings.answer: Contact support with the account email, order reference, job reference, package or tool name, and a short description of what happened. Those details help the team locate the generation request, credit reservation, payment event, or private gallery record faster.

settings.question: What information should I include when reporting a bad result?
settings.answer: Include the page or tool you used, the package direction, the approximate request time, and what looks wrong in the output, such as identity mismatch, crop issue, missing download, image artifact, or video motion problem. Do not send extra private source photos unless support asks for a specific reference.

settings.question: Can support review credits, failed jobs, or refund questions?
settings.answer: Support can review visible checkout records, credit reservations, settled credits, released credits, failed-request states, and private delivery status tied to the signed-in account. Refund eligibility still follows the current Refund Policy, Terms of Service, and the recorded order status.

settings.question: Where can I read the rules before uploading photos?
settings.answer: Use the Privacy Policy, Content Policy, Terms of Service, Refund Policy, and Cookie Policy before uploading source photos, buying credits, or publishing outputs. These pages explain privacy, acceptable content, billing, refund, and site-use rules.

settings.question: Should I send private source photos through email or chat?
settings.answer: Avoid sending unnecessary private photos through external channels. The workspace is the preferred place for source photos and private generation records; support usually needs identifiers and a description before any additional image reference.

settings.question: What if my request involves another person, a brand, or sensitive content?
settings.answer: Only upload photos you own or have permission to use, and make sure every person shown has approved the intended use. Avoid misleading endorsements, protected logos, public-figure likeness issues, sensitive contexts, or content that violates the Content Policy.

seo.title: myDreamshoots KIDS Act
seo.description: Read the myDreamshoots children's privacy notice for COPPA-aware account access, minor image uploads, parent or guardian requests, and private gallery handling.

settings.body:
1. Service audience

myDreamshoots is not directed to children under 13 and is not designed for child account creation. Customers should use the service only if they can lawfully manage an account or have permission from a parent or legal guardian.

2. COPPA-aware handling

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. myDreamshoots does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. DPDPA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our DPDPA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

6. Contact

Email support@test.grownstride.com for children's privacy or COPPA-related questions.

settings.title: Cookie policy

settings.body: This policy explains the cookies and local storage used on test.grownstride.com for the MydreamShoots AI photo service.
settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. MydreamShoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps MydreamShoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, MydreamShoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@test.grownstride.com with cookie or tracking questions.

Refund requests should be submitted within 30 days of the purchase date. If a subscription is canceled, the customer keeps access to purchased credits until they are used or expire according to plan rules. Cancellation does not automatically refund credits already used.

seo.keywords: myDreamshoots policy, AI photo privacy, AI portrait terms, photo upload privacy, private AI albums, AI photo credits, no AI training, 30-day auto-delete, AES-256
seo.description: Read how myDreamshoots keeps account data, uploaded source photos, generated portraits, credit activity, checkout records, and private album access private. Your photos are never used to train models, input photos auto-delete 30 days after generation, and data is protected with AES-256 at rest and TLS 256-bit in transit.

settings.body:
1. Scope of this policy

This Privacy Policy explains how myDreamshoots handles customer accounts, uploaded source photos, generated portraits, prompts, credit activity, checkout records, cookies, support messages, and private album access.

2. No AI training on your photos

Your uploaded photos, prompts, and generated private results are used to provide the myDreamshoots service you request. They are never used to train models or build public datasets.

3. 30-day auto-delete for input photos

Input photos automatically delete 30 days after generation. Generated results, billing records, security logs, dispute records, and support messages may be retained where needed for account access, legal compliance, fraud prevention, refunds, and customer support.

4. AES-256 at rest · TLS 256-bit in transit

myDreamshoots protects private uploads and account data with AES-256 at rest and TLS 256-bit in transit across the stack. Access checks, scoped sessions, security cookies, monitoring, and provider controls reduce unauthorized access.

5. Payments, credits, and service providers

Payments may be processed by Stripe or another connected provider. Hosting, storage, email, moderation, analytics, payment, and AI infrastructure providers may process limited data only to run, secure, generate, store, or deliver the requested service.

6. Compliance references

Our footer links include KIDS Act and DPDPA notices because privacy, child-related requests, deletion, access, correction, and regional privacy rights matter for AI photo services.

7. Your choices and contact

You may ask for access, correction, export, deletion, or help with account privacy. Email support@test.grownstride.com with your account email and request details. We may verify account ownership before acting on sensitive requests.

settings.question: What photos should I upload?
settings.answer: Use recent, sharp photos where your face is visible and not heavily filtered. A small set of varied source images usually gives the workflow more useful information than many near-duplicates.
settings.body: Good source photos do not need to be professional studio images. Natural phone photos can work well when the subject is well lit, unobstructed, and captured from several useful angles.
settings.bulletList: Use clear focus and even lighting|Include front, three-quarter, and natural-expression views|Avoid sunglasses, extreme filters, heavy blur, and cropped faces|Include wardrobe or hairstyle variety when the package calls for it
settings.imageAlt: Clear source portrait showing the sharp lighting and visible face recommended for myDreamshoots AI photo uploads

settings.question: Can I create couple or group photos?
settings.answer: Yes. Couple, friend, and group results work best when every person is clearly visible in approved source photos and the chosen package is designed for more than one subject.
settings.body: For a group set, keep the source images organized and make sure each person has given permission for the intended use. Results can vary when faces are small, hidden, or heavily overlapping.
settings.bulletList: Get permission from every person shown|Use clear group and individual reference photos|Choose a package that supports the number of subjects|Review faces and hands before sharing

settings.question: What can the Best AI Image page help me create?
settings.answer: The Best AI Image page helps you compare private AI image directions such as profile photos, professional portraits, creator images, seasonal albums, fashion concepts, beauty previews, product lifestyle shots, and social-ready visuals generated from approved source photos.

settings.question: How do I choose the best AI image theme for my use case?
settings.answer: Choose by destination and intent. LinkedIn headshots need a cleaner professional look, creator campaigns need expressive crops, seasonal cards need clear holiday context, and business or product images need realistic framing that matches the channel where the image will appear.

settings.question: Which source photos produce the best AI image results?
settings.answer: Use sharp, recent, well-lit photos with visible faces or subjects, natural skin detail, and minimal obstruction. Avoid heavy filters, screenshots, low-resolution crops, copyrighted references, and images of people who have not approved the intended use.

settings.question: Are AI image results private by default?
settings.answer: Generated image requests are tied to the signed-in myDreamshoots account and delivered through the private workspace or gallery. The images are not treated as a public portfolio by default, but privacy also depends on what you choose to download and share.

settings.question: Can I use generated AI images on profiles, social media, or business pages?
settings.answer: You can use suitable results when you control the source material, have permission from every person shown, follow platform rules, and include any required AI disclosure. Review commercial claims, endorsements, logos, and sensitive contexts before publishing.

settings.question: How should I review final AI images before download?
settings.answer: Check face identity, hands, teeth, eyes, text-like marks, background artifacts, clothing details, brand marks, and crop quality. Keep the strongest outputs and avoid using images that could misrepresent a person, location, product, or affiliation.
